content.value_statement: React Effects are often used for state that can be calculated during render, creating extra renders and bugs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward safer useEffect patterns and better React alternatives.
actual_capabilities: Explains when a React component needs an Effect for external synchronization.
Identifies useEffect anti-patterns such as derived state, Effect chains, and event-specific logic.
Recommends alternatives such as render-time calculations, useMemo, key props, and event handlers.
Shows data-fetching cleanup patterns that reduce stale responses and race conditions.
Provides a decision tree and reference tables for reviewing React hook code.
limitations: It is guidance-only and does not execute tests or inspect a running React app.
It focuses on useEffect decisions, not a full React architecture review.
Examples use simplified components and may need adaptation for a production framework.
It does not replace framework data-loading tools such as Next.js loaders or React Query.

use_cases.title: Refactor overused Effects
use_cases.description: Find Effects that only derive state, reset local state, or respond to user actions.

use_cases.title: Review pull requests
use_cases.description: Check hook usage for stale values, missing cleanup, unnecessary state, and fragile Effect chains.

use_cases.title: Standardize React patterns
use_cases.description: Teach teams when to use render calculations, event handlers, useMemo, key props, and custom hooks.

prompt_templates.title: Decide if an Effect is needed
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a single component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component and tell me whether it needs useEffect. Explain the simplest alternative if an Effect is unnecessary.

prompt_templates.title: Fix derived state
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate refactor for state copied from props or other state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find any derived state updated by useEffect in this component. Recommend a render-time calculation or useMemo when the calculation is expensive.

prompt_templates.title: Review cleanup and races
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for data fetching, timers, or subscriptions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Effects for missing cleanup, stale responses, and React Strict Mode issues. Suggest safe cleanup patterns and framework alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign Effect-heavy flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this React flow for Effect chains and state synchronization problems. Propose a simpler design using event handlers, lifted state, keys, or custom hooks.

output_examples.input: A form stores a full name in state and updates it whenever first name or last name changes.
output: Finding: The Effect is unnecessary because the full name is derived from existing state.
Recommendation: Calculate the full name during render so the UI avoids an extra stale render.
Risk reduced: Fewer state updates and simpler dependency management.

output_examples.input: A search component fetches results when the query changes and sometimes shows old results.
output: Finding: The Effect needs cleanup because older requests can finish after newer requests.
Recommendation: Ignore stale responses, cancel requests when possible, or use a framework data-loading tool.
Risk reduced: The UI is less likely to show results for an outdated query.

best_practices: Ask whether an external system is involved before adding an Effect.
Calculate values during render when they come from existing props or state.
Return cleanup from Effects that subscribe, fetch, set timers, or touch external resources.
anti_patterns: Do not store derived values in state only to update them from an Effect.
Do not use Effects for logic that belongs in a click, submit, or change handler.
Do not chain Effects that update state only to trigger more Effects.

faq.question: When should I use useEffect?
faq.answer: Use useEffect when a component must synchronize with something outside React, such as a browser API or subscription.

faq.question: When should I avoid useEffect?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the value can be calculated during render or when the logic belongs to a user event.

faq.question: Does this skill replace React Query or framework loaders?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend those tools, but it does not replace framework data-loading features.

faq.question: Can it help with race conditions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains cleanup flags, stale response handling, and when framework data loading is safer.

faq.question: Does it support React Strict Mode?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance explains why Effects run twice in development and how cleanup exposes missing logic.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill during reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill gives review prompts and patterns for detecting unnecessary or fragile Effects.
